author: TeIq
content:
## Source
.design/m5/48-tpm-signing.md — full design.

## What this epic delivers
Fifth `SigningKey` impl using TPM 2.0 PCR-bound sealing. K-256 keypair generated INSIDE the TPM; private key never leaves. Restart is zero-touch; unseal succeeds only on the original hardware in the original boot state. Defends T1-T3 fully and T4 partially (process can call TPM sign API but cannot exfiltrate key material).

## Hard constraints
- **No hand-written `unsafe`** in `polaris-backend/src/labeler/signer/tpm.rs`. All FFI lives inside `tss-esapi`. If a path requires `unsafe`, upstream the safe wrapper.
- **miri test mandatory** for any module touching `tss-esapi`. Per rust-quality §5 (unsafe discipline).
- **Linux only** in v2. macOS Secure Enclave + Windows TPM are future issues.

## Sub-issues (8 PRs + 1 Q-resolution)
- Q-resolution: tss-esapi maturity (Q1), curve choice (Q2), recovery auth (Q3), HA story (Q4), multi-tenant TPM (Q5)
- PR 1: 1-2 day spike verifying `tss-esapi` maturity + curve support against Bluesky verifier
- PR 2: `TpmSigningKey` impl skeleton + `TpmError` enum + soft-TPM (`swtpm`) fixture test; AC-1
- PR 3: PCR-policy sealing (PCR0/4/7 default); AC-2 + AC-7
- PR 4: `polaris labeler-key init --mode tpm --pcrs 0,4,7` admin command; AC-3
- PR 5: `polaris labeler-key rotate` TPM-mode extension; AC-6
- PR 6: `polaris labeler-key reseal-after-update` with offline sealing-auth token (Q3-A); AC-5
- PR 7: `docs/operations/tpm-signing.md` operator runbook
- PR 8: miri + unsafe audit closure (AC-8)

## Provisional answers
- Q1: implementer verifies tss-esapi current state in PR 1 spike. Fallback: cryptoki + software-TPM PKCS#11 module.
- Q2: C (support both K-256 and P-256 via `did:key` curve declaration) IF Bluesky verifier supports both; otherwise A (K-256 only).
- Q3: A (offline sealing-auth token) — matches the strength of TPM sealing.
- Q4: A (single-host-TPM only; HA-needing operators use cloud-kms-oracle).
- Q5: documentation-only; operator allocates a TPM hierarchy for Polaris.

## Rust-quality notes for downstream
- **`SigningKey` trait conformance**: per rust-quality §1, the new impl satisfies the existing v1 trait verbatim. Callers (emit, rotate, declare) are unchanged.
- **`TpmError` is `thiserror`** with structured variants per design REQ-5: `Unavailable`, `SealPolicyMismatch { found_pcrs, sealed_pcrs }`, `PcrUpdateRequired`, `HandleNotFound`, `SigningFailed(#[from] tss_esapi::Error)`.
- **TPM session lifetime**: an `Esys_Context` opened at startup, kept alive for the process. Per rust-quality §10: Drop impl flushes the session cleanly on shutdown. NEVER hold an Esys_Context across `await` boundaries — TPM operations are synchronous; wrap in `tokio::task::spawn_blocking` if called from async code.
- **K-256 / P-256 curve dispatch**: at-startup detection. The `did:key` published in `app.bsky.labeler.service` encodes the curve. Per rust-quality §1: encode this in a `pub enum CurveChoice { K256, P256 }` newtype, not a string.
- **Process-memory hygiene**: per AC-2, no private key in process memory. The TPM handle is an Esys reference; the public key extracted at startup is the only key-derived bytes in memory. Document this in the impl's doc-comment.
- Per rust-quality §7: integration test against `swtpm` (software TPM) in CI. Mark with `#[ignore]` and run via `cargo test -- --ignored` so CI without TPM hardware can still verify.

## External references
- `tss-esapi`: https://docs.rs/tss-esapi/latest/tss_esapi/
- TPM 2.0 spec: https://trustedcomputinggroup.org/resource/tpm-library-specification/
- `swtpm` for fixture testing: https://github.com/stefanberger/swtpm
- TCG PCR usage: https://uapi-group.org/specifications/specs/linux_tpm_pcr_registry/
- v1 SigningKey trait + four existing impls: `polaris-backend/src/labeler/signer/`

## Blocks / blocked-by
- Independent of all other M5 epics. The `cloud-kms-oracle` mode (v1) and #153 hardware-token mode are complementary signing modes, not alternatives.
